text: Somnath Bharti, born on 10 May 1974, is an Indian politician and lawyer. He is a member of the Aam Aadmi Party and served as a Member of Legislative Assembly (MLA) from the Malviya Nagar constituency in Delhi from 2013 until 2025. He previously held the position of Minister of Law, Tourism, Administrative Reforms, Art & Culture in the Government of Delhi from 28 December 2013 to 14 February 2014 in the first Arvind Kejriwal government, which resigned due to its failure to pass the Jan Lokpal bill. Bharti is a practicing lawyer in the Supreme Court of India and the Delhi High Court. He was born into a Baranwal Bania family in Hisua Bazar, Nawada, and received his early education at a local school before studying intermediate in Patna. He completed his post-graduate M.Sc. in Mathematics from IIT Delhi and later earned a law degree from Delhi University. He served in various leadership roles within the IIT Delhi Alumni Association, including Secretary (2007–08 and 2011–12), President of IIT DAA (2012–13), and IIT Delhi Senator (2008). In the 2000s, he ran a Delhi-based IT firm, Madgen Solutions, and was named in the Spamhaus Project’s Register of Known Spam Operations (ROKSO) as one of the top spam operators, following an Open Directory Project story by Conrad Longmore. PCQuest found that he had been sued in California Superior Court for spamming by Daniel Balsam, and Balsam’s attorney revealed that in 2004, Bharti and two others paid damages and agreed to use only opt-in email addresses. Bharti claimed he settled to avoid higher legal costs and stated he had contact with SpamHaus, though SpamHaus CEO Steve Linford denied this. In 2009, he represented Vikram Buddhi and led a movement against the abeyance of sentencing in the U.S. In 2013, he advocated for the quashing of a FIR against eight accused in the Constable Tomar's death during the Nirbhaya protests, citing video footage and witness accounts to argue their innocence. In June 2012, he campaigned against alleged interference by Kapil Sibal in the Joint Entrance Examination process. Between 2010 and 2013, he filed three Public Interest Litigations in the Delhi High Court defending the rights of homeschooled children and alternate education system subscribers, prompting the Ministry of Human Resources and Development to clarify it was not against homeschooling. Bharti contested and won the Malviya Nagar seat in the 2013 Delhi assembly elections, defeating Arti Mehra of the Bharatiya Janata Party and incumbent Kiran Walia of the Indian National Congress, who had previously won the seat in 1999, 2003, and 2008 and served as education minister. Bharti was Chairman of the Committee on Privileges of the Delhi Legislative Assembly in 2016–17 and was appointed Chairman of the Committee to examine the stray dog and monkey menace in Delhi on 10 August 2018. He won the 2020 Delhi Elections by a margin of 18,144 votes and was appointed Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee, Chairman of the House Committee on Violation of Protocol Norms and Contemptuous Behaviour by Government Officers with MLAs, and member of the Standing Committee on Education and the Committee on Govt Undertakings. In February 2015, he won the seat by double the margin of his previous victory, with the AAP securing 67 out of 70 Delhi assembly seats. He was appointed to the Delhi Development Authority (DDA) board, where his efforts led to the recovery of over 65,000 unclaimed and encroached lands across Delhi. In March 2023, he was appointed Vice Chairman of the Delhi Jal Board. After being elected MLA, he initiated a direct dialogue program using "mohalla groups" on WhatsApp. In the 2025 Delhi Legislative Assembly election, he lost the Malviya Nagar seat by a margin of 2,131 votes to BJP candidate Satish Upadhyay. In 2013, the Patiala House Court indicted Bharti for "tampering with evidence" in a corruption case alongside his client Pawan Kumar, and he was asked by the Bar Council of Delhi to explain why he should not be debarred. In January 2014, less than a month after being elected, Bharti led a vigilante raid in Khirki Extension, allegedly targeting a drug and prostitution racket involving African nationals. He quarreled with the Station House Officer, who refused the raid without a warrant, and the group reportedly forced four women to undergo urine tests at AIIMS, which found no drug traces. The women alleged they were threatened and molested. Protests followed, with the BJP and CPM condemning Bharti's actions as racist and criticizing the mob for violating the women. AAP defended Bharti, calling the allegations false and stating residents had long complained of criminal activity. Kejriwal demanded the suspension of the police officers who refused the raid, and a court directed the police to file a First Information Report against the mob, while the Delhi Commission for Women opened an investigation. Kejriwal's government faced increasing political pressure before its resignation, and an independent judicial inquiry ordered by the Lieutenant Governor on 28 February 2014 concluded that the police had acted correctly and that Bharti had improperly taken the law into his own hands. Around two years later, The Hindu reported that the raid led to an "exodus" of African nationals and emboldened locals to abuse and taunt the remaining ones. In June 2015, Bharti's wife filed a complaint with the Delhi Commission for Women alleging domestic violence. On 29 September 2015, Bharti surrendered at the Dwarka Police Station under Supreme Court directions and obtained conditional bail. He claimed the couple resolved the dispute through mediation, but the court charged him with harassment, cheating, and criminal intimidation. In May 2019, the Delhi High Court quashed the FIR, noting the couple was living happily together. In 2021, Bharti was sentenced to two years in prison for leading a mob into AIIMS Delhi, claiming there was no evidence and the case was based on a fabricated story. The Delhi High Court stayed the judgment and granted him bail.
